notes.title: Calculus of a Single Variable — complete revision notes

sections.heading: Limits & Continuity
bullets: lim f(x) = L means both one-sided limits exist and equal L — check left and right separately at break points.
Standard limits: lim sinθ/θ = 1 (θ→0), lim (1+θ)^{1/θ} = e, lim (e^θ−1)/θ = 1.
f is continuous at a iff lim_{x→a} f = f(a); discontinuities are removable, jump, or infinite.
Sandwich theorem rescues messy limits: g(x) ≤ f(x) ≤ h(x) and both ends converge ⇒ f converges.

sections.heading: Differentiability
bullets: f′(a) = lim_{h→0} (f(a+h)−f(a))/h — existence requires left derivative = right derivative.
Differentiable ⇒ continuous, but NOT conversely: f(x)=|x| is continuous at 0, not differentiable.
Rules: (uv)′ = u′v + uv′, (u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v², chain rule d/dx f(g) = f′(g)·g′.
L'Hôpital's rule: only for 0/0 or ∞/∞ forms — differentiate numerator and denominator separately.
Mean Value Theorem: f continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b) ⇒ ∃c with f′(c) = (f(b)−f(a))/(b−a).

sections.heading: Applications & series
bullets: Maxima/minima: solve f′(x)=0, classify with f″(x) (concave up = min, down = max) or sign chart.
Taylor/Maclaurin: f(x) = Σ f⁽ⁿ⁾(0) xⁿ/n! — memorise eˣ, sin x, cos x, ln(1+x), (1+x)ⁿ expansions.
Curve sketching: monotonicity from f′ sign, concavity from f″ sign, asymptotes from limits.

sections.heading: Integration
bullets: Indefinite integrals: ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) (n≠−1), ∫dx/x = ln|x|, ∫eˣ dx = eˣ.
Techniques: substitution (reverse chain rule), by parts ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du, partial fractions for rational functions.
Definite integral = net area; Fundamental Theorem: ∫ₐᵇ f = F(b) − F(a) where F′ = f.
Improper integrals: take limits before evaluating; check convergence at ∞ and at singular points.

questions.prompt: Is f(x) = |x| differentiable at x = 0? Justify.
solution: Limits differ ⇒ derivative does not exist (function is still continuous).
By parts: u = x, dv = eˣ dx ⇒ du = dx, v = eˣ.
∫ x eˣ dx = x eˣ − ∫ eˣ dx.
= x eˣ − eˣ + C = eˣ(x−1) + C.

notes.title: Calculus of Several Variables — revision notes

sections.heading: Partial derivatives
bullets: ∂f/∂x differentiates f with respect to x holding all other variables constant.
Total differential: df = (∂f/∂x)dx + (∂f/∂y)dy — the linear approximation engine.
Chain rule for z = f(u,v) with u(t), v(t): dz/dt = f_u·u′ + f_v·v′.
Clairaut's theorem: if f_xy and f_yx are continuous they are equal — mixed partials commute.

sections.heading: Extrema & Lagrange
bullets: Critical points: ∇f = 0; classify with D = f_xx·f_yy − f_xy² (D>0 & f_xx>0 min, D>0 & f_xx<0 max, D<0 saddle).
Constrained extrema: Lagrange ∇f = λ∇g — solve alongside g(x,y)=c.
Chain of errors: Δz ≈ f_x Δx + f_y Δy for estimation problems.

sections.heading: Implicit & directional
bullets: Implicit differentiation: dy/dx = −F_x/F_y for F(x,y)=0.
Directional derivative = ∇f · û — maximum in the gradient direction, |∇f| is its value.
Gradient is perpendicular to level curves; tangent to the curve has slope −F_x/F_y.

questions.prompt: f(x,y) = x³y + xy². Find f_x and f_y at (1,2).
Classify the critical point of f(x,y) = x² + y² − 6x + 4y + 13.
solution: D = f_xx f_yy − f_xy² = 2·2 − 0 = 4 > 0, f_xx = 2 > 0 ⇒ minimum.

questions.prompt: Use Lagrange to minimise f(x,y) = x + y subject to x² + y² = 1.
z = f(u,v), u = t², v = sin t. Write dz/dt.
solution: Chain rule for two intermediate variables.

sections.heading: Double integrals
bullets: ∫∫_R f dA: iterate — inner integral first, outer last; sketch R every single time.
Type-I region: y from y₁(x) to y₂(x); Type-II: x from x₁(y) to x₂(y) — choose the simpler order.
Fubini holds when f is continuous on a rectangular region: dA = dx dy or dy dx.

sections.heading: Polar coordinates
bullets: x = r cosθ, y = r sinθ, dA = r dr dθ (never forget the Jacobian r).
Circles, petals and annuli become trivial in polar: r from 0 to a, θ from 0 to 2π.
General Jacobian: dA = |∂(x,y)/∂(u,v)| du dv for any substitution.

sections.heading: Triple integrals & applications
bullets: Triple ∫∫∫ f dz dy dx over a solid — use cylindrical (extra r) or spherical coordinates for symmetry.
Mass = ∫∫ ρ dA, centroid (x̄,ȳ) = (1/A)∫∫ x dA, (1/A)∫∫ y dA.
Area of R = ∫∫_R dA; volume = ∫∫∫ dV — set limits from the region description, not memory.

questions.prompt: Express ∫∫_R (x²+y²) dA over the disk x²+y² ≤ 4 in polar and evaluate.
solution: Polar: x²+y² = r², dA = r dr dθ.
Circle of radius 1 centred at (1,0); θ from −π/2 to π/2.
A = ½∫ r² dθ = ½ ∫_{−π/2}^{π/2} 4cos²θ dθ = 2 · (π/2) = π.

sections.heading: Matrix basics
bullets: AB ≠ BA in general; (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ; (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹.
Row operations → echelon form → rank = number of non-zero rows.
det(AB) = det(A)det(B); det(A⁻¹) = 1/det(A); swapping rows flips the sign.

sections.heading: Systems & rank
bullets: Ax = b is consistent iff rank(A) = rank(A|b).
Unique solution iff rank = number of unknowns; infinitely many if rank < n; none if ranks differ.
Cramer's rule works only for square systems with det ≠ 0 — prefer elimination in practice.

sections.heading: Eigenvalues
bullets: Characteristic equation det(A − λI) = 0; eigenvectors satisfy (A − λI)v = 0.
Sum of eigenvalues = trace(A), product = det(A) — instant sanity checks.
Diagonalisable iff you can collect n independent eigenvectors; A = PDP⁻¹ gives Aᵏ = PDᵏP⁻¹.

sections.heading: Exam traps
bullets: Never divide a row by zero — swap rows first.
A singular matrix has no inverse; det = 0 ⇔ columns linearly dependent.
